q: Which channel sizes break out most, and are their audiences happy? Give n.
a:
Small channels break out most, and mid-size channels have the happiest audiences.

- Small: 34.6% of videos outperformed their baseline (n=52 videos), with an average lift of about 5.4x. Net sentiment is +24 (49% positive, 24% negative; n=500 product-side comments).
- Mid: 23.1% outperformed (n=39), with a lift of about 1.6x. Net sentiment is +33 (53% positive, 20% negative; n=453).
- Large: 5.3% outperformed (n=19), with a lift of about 1.0x. Net sentiment is +12 (45% positive, 32% negative; n=217).

Large channels both rarely break out and have the least happy audiences. Caveat: the large group has only 19 videos, so its rate could shift a lot with a few videos.
sql:
WITH v AS (
 SELECT c.video_id, p.outperformer, p.rel_lift,
 CASE WHEN cr.tier IN ('nano <50k','micro 50-250k') THEN 'small'
 WHEN cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' THEN 'mid'
 WHEN cr.tier IN ('macro 1-5M','mega 5M+') THEN 'large' END AS size_group
 FROM content c
 JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id
 JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id
 WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official'
),
perf AS (
 SELECT size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_videos_with_baseline,
 ROUND(AVG(outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate,
 ROUND(AVG(rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift
 FROM v WHERE outperformer IS NOT NULL AND size_group IS NOT NULL
 GROUP BY size_group
),
sent AS (
 SELECT v.size_group, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side_comments,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative,
 ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS net_sentiment
 FROM v JOIN comments m ON m.video_id=v.video_id
 WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor')
 AND v.outperformer IS NOT NULL AND v.size_group IS NOT NULL
 GROUP BY v.size_group
)
SELECT perf.size_group, perf.n_videos_with_baseline, perf.outperformer_rate, perf.avg_rel_lift,
 sent.n_product_side_comments, sent.pct_positive, sent.pct_negative,
 CASE WHEN sent.n_product_side_comments>=10 THEN sent.net_sentiment END AS net_sentiment
FROM perf LEFT JOIN sent USING(size_group)
ORDER BY perf.outperformer_rate DESC
LIMIT 40

q: Which content formats work best for mid-sized channels?
a:
First impressions work best for mid-sized channels. Across 18 videos, they average a relative lift of 2.38, and 44% (about 8 of 18) were outperformers. Net sentiment is +37 (n=231 product-side comments).

Explainer tips are a distant second: 6 videos, lift 1.13, 17% outperformers, net sentiment +20 (n=70).

Comparisons show a decent lift of 1.70 but no outperformers, and only 3 videos, so treat that as tentative. Net sentiment is +18 (n=45).

Upgrade advice drew warm reactions (+46, n=54) but had a low lift of 0.65 and no outperformers (6 videos).

Keynote recaps (2 videos), "other" (3) and meme shorts (1) have too few videos to judge. None had an outperformer.

Caveat: these are associations, not causes, and the comments are only a sample.
sql: WITH v AS (SELECT c.video_id, c.format, p.rel_lift, p.outperformer FROM content c JOIN creators cr ON cr.channel_id=c.channel_id JOIN performance p ON p.video_id=c.video_id WHERE c.topic='duo' AND c.format!='official' AND cr.tier='mid 250k-1M' AND p.rel_lift IS NOT NULL), s AS (SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_comments, SUM(cm.sentiment='positive') AS pos, SUM(cm.sentiment='negative') AS neg FROM v JOIN comments cm ON cm.video_id=v.video_id WHERE cm.lang='en' AND cm.trivial=0 AND cm.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') GROUP BY v.format) SELECT v.format, COUNT(*) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(v.rel_lift),3) AS avg_rel_lift, ROUND(AVG(v.outperformer),3) AS outperformer_rate, s.n_comments AS n_product_side_comments, CASE WHEN s.n_comments>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(s.pos-s.neg)/s.n_comments,3) END AS net_sentiment FROM v LEFT JOIN s ON s.format=v.format GROUP BY v.format ORDER BY outperformer_rate DESC, avg_rel_lift DESC LIMIT 40

q: Which high-lift videos have the most negative audience reaction? Name two examples, with lift and sentiment shown separately.
a:
Only two videos qualified, both from Shawn Shaman, and neither is strongly negative. Sentiment is mixed to slightly negative.

1. "Apple Tricked You With iPhone Duo" (meme short): lift 118.45 (relative lift 9.51), 181,226 views. Net sentiment is -7 (43% positive, 50% negative, n=14).

2. "Don't Buy The #iPhoneDuo... Here's Why" (upgrade advice): lift 135.84 (relative lift 10.91), 207,839 views. Net sentiment is 0 (31% positive, 31% negative, n=16).

Both samples are small, so a few comments could move these scores a lot. Because both videos come from one channel, this may reflect that creator's audience rather than high-lift Duo videos in general.
sql: SELECT v.video_id, v.title, c.name AS channel, v.format, v.views, ROUND(v.lift,3) AS lift, ROUND(v.rel_lift,3) AS rel_lift, v.outperformer, v.n_product_side, ROUND(v.pct_positive,3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(v.pct_negative,3) AS pct_negative, ROUND(v.pct_positive - v.pct_negative,3) AS net_sentiment FROM v_content v JOIN creators c ON c.channel_id = v.channel_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND v.outperformer=1 AND v.n_product_side>=10 ORDER BY net_sentiment ASC, v.rel_lift DESC LIMIT 2

q: Which audience topics are largest, and which are growing fastest this week?
a:
The largest topics overall are Praise for the video (n=208, 9.3% of comments), Samsung Fold comparisons (n=143, 6.4%), High price (n=131, 5.9%), Cases and design (n=114, 5.1%), and Eager to buy (n=104, 4.7%).

Samsung Fold comparisons is growing fastest: 15 comments the prior week to 70 this week (+367%). Next are High price and Cases and design, each rising from 17 to 57 (+235%). Then come Apple's approach and Android (15 to 44, +193%) and Reasons not to buy (10 to 28, +180%).

Several topics rose sharply from small bases, so no growth rate is shown. Buy or don't buy went from 6 to 33, Pre-order plans from 9 to 33, and Left-handed concerns from 4 to 22. These are small counts.

Caveat: this reflects a sample of comments, not all viewers. The result has no sentiment data.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.topic_id, c.day_since_launch AS d FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id WHERE v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0), mx AS (SELECT MAX(d) AS m FROM base), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS t FROM base), agg AS (SELECT b.topic_id, COUNT(*) AS n_total, SUM(CASE WHEN b.d > mx.m-7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_this_week, SUM(CASE WHEN b.d <= mx.m-7 AND b.d > mx.m-14 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS n_prev_week FROM base b, mx WHERE b.topic_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.topic_id) SELECT t.topic_id, t.name, t.pool, t.origin, t.first_seen, a.n_total, ROUND(1.0*a.n_total/tot.t,3) AS share_of_comments, a.n_this_week, a.n_prev_week, CASE WHEN a.n_prev_week>=10 THEN ROUND(1.0*(a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week)/a.n_prev_week,3) END AS wow_growth, a.n_this_week-a.n_prev_week AS wow_change, (SELECT m FROM mx) AS latest_day FROM agg a JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=a.topic_id, tot ORDER BY a.n_total DESC LIMIT 40

q: How does audience sentiment on the main product compare with the other products in the data?
a:
Duo sentiment is clearly better than every other topic, with a net score of +25 (n=1,426 product-side comments across 127 videos). About 49% are positive, 28% neutral and 24% negative.

The other topics are far smaller and less favorable:
- General event videos: net -14.5 (n=76, 8 videos), with 26% positive and 41% negative.
- Other: net -10 (n=51, 6 videos), with 31% positive and 41% negative.
- Competitor foldables: net 0 (n=27, 2 videos), with 37% positive and 37% negative.
- iPhone 18 Pro: only 4 comments from 1 video, so no net score is reported and it can't be compared.

Caveat: the non-Duo groups have small samples, so treat their scores as rough. These are comments from a sample of videos, not all viewers.
sql: SELECT c.topic, COUNT(*) AS n_product_side, COUNT(DISTINCT c.video_id) AS n_videos, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive'),3) AS pct_positive, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='neutral'),3) AS pct_neutral, ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) AS pct_negative, CASE WHEN COUNT(*)>=10 THEN ROUND(AVG(m.sentiment='positive')-AVG(m.sentiment='negative'),3) END AS net_sentiment FROM comments m JOIN content c ON c.video_id=m.video_id WHERE m.lang='en' AND m.trivial=0 AND m.target IN ('product','price_value','competitor') AND c.format!='official' GROUP BY c.topic ORDER BY (c.topic='duo') DESC, n_product_side DESC LIMIT 40

q: What do people like most about iPhone Duo, and what do they criticise most?
a:
People like the fold animation most. Net sentiment there is +70 (n=56), with 84% positive and 14% negative. Commenters call it smooth and very Apple. Eagerness to buy is next at +38 (n=104), as many say they plan to order one.

Price draws the most criticism. Net sentiment is +3 (n=131), with 39% positive and 36% negative. It accounts for 14% of all negative comments (47 negative comments). Commenters call the phone overpriced, and many joke about the high-end model's cost. The Duo versus iPhone 18 Pro Max debate is also split, at +2 (n=101), with some choosing to wait or buy the Pro Max.

Samsung Fold comparisons have the most comments (n=143, +29), and they mix praise with criticism.

Caveat: this is a comment sample, and topics overlap, so shares don't add up cleanly.
sql: WITH base AS (SELECT c.comment_id, c.sentiment, t.topic_id, t.name, t.summary FROM comments c JOIN content v ON v.video_id=c.video_id JOIN topics t ON t.topic_id=c.topic_id WHERE c.lang='en' AND c.trivial=0 AND v.topic='duo' AND v.format!='official' AND t.pool='product' AND c.target IN ('product','price_value','apple_brand','competitor')), agg AS (SELECT topic_id, name, summary, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(sentiment='positive') AS n_pos, SUM(sentiment='negative') AS n_neg FROM base GROUP BY topic_id, name, summary), tot AS (SELECT a.*, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/n,3) AS pct_pos, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/n,3) AS pct_neg, ROUND(1.0*n_pos/(SELECT SUM(n_pos) FROM agg),3) AS share_of_all_pos, ROUND(1.0*n_neg/(SELECT SUM(n_neg) FROM agg),3) AS share_of_all_neg FROM agg a) SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'most_liked' AS side, topic_id, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg, share_of_all_pos, share_of_all_neg FROM tot ORDER BY n_pos DESC LIMIT 6) UNION ALL SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'most_criticised' AS side, topic_id, name, summary, n, n_pos, n_neg, pct_pos, pct_neg, share_of_all_pos, share_of_all_neg FROM tot ORDER BY n_neg DESC LIMIT 6)
